headline: EU forced labour guidelines, revised ESRS, and battery passport preparations
summary: The European Commission has published official guidelines under the Forced Labour Regulation, while streamlined ESRS reporting standards and supplier data limits were finalised. Technical preparations for the Digital Battery Passport continue to advance, and EU lawmakers are progressing discussions to potentially extend CBAM to downstream finished goods.

items.title: Commission publishes official Forced Labour Regulation guidelines
items.what: The European Commission has released official implementation guidelines for the EU Forced Labour Regulation, detailing due diligence expectations and enforcement criteria for international supply chains.
items.meaning: Critical for your Chinese manufacturing base. Authorities will use these benchmarks to investigate forced labour risks, requiring robust evidence of supply chain tracing.
items.action: Audit Chinese Tier-1 and component suppliers against the new guidance to identify labour compliance vulnerabilities.

sources.title: Update on the EU Forced Labour Regulation: The European Commission's Guidelines Have Been Published

items.title: EU finalises revised ESRS and caps supplier data requests
items.what: The EU finalised streamlined reporting standards, with rules introduced allowing suppliers with up to 1,000 staff to reject excessive sustainability data demands exceeding standard metrics.
items.meaning: Ahead of your financial year 2027 CSRD reporting, you must ensure data requests sent to Chinese manufacturing partners remain strictly within standardised limits.
items.action: Align your supply chain ESG data requests with the final streamlined ESRS and voluntary SME standards.

sources.title: Brussels Sets a Data Ceiling: Suppliers With Up to 1,000 Staff Can Now Refuse Extra Sustainability R

items.title: Digital Battery Passport certification rolls out ahead of deadlines
items.what: TÜV SÜD launched Digital Battery Passport certification services, and industry brands are accelerating implementation ahead of mandatory EU requirements.
items.meaning: Your proprietary battery platform will require certified digital passports covering raw material sources, recycled content, and lifecycle emissions.
items.action: Map battery pack technical data with Chinese cell suppliers to ensure readiness for battery passport verification.

sources.title: TÜV SÜD launches Digital Battery Passport certification

items.title: Proposed CBAM downstream extension advances toward trilogue talks
items.what: Draft proposals to extend CBAM to downstream finished products and enforce anti-circumvention provisions are progressing toward EU inter-institutional trilogue negotiations.
items.meaning: Currently only proposed, but if adopted, importing finished metal tools could eventually fall within scope despite your current exemption from basic material imports.
items.action: Track downstream tariff codes under discussion to assess potential long-term cost exposure on finished power tools.
